stem:
Omar looks at the diagram of $\triangle PQR$ with $\angle P = 55^{\circ}$ and $\angle PQR = 65^{\circ}$. Side $PQ$ is extended to $S$, so $\angle RQS = x$.

Which claim finds $x$ correctly?

options.text: $x = 115^{\circ}$, because $\angle PQR = 65^{\circ}$ and $x$ forms a straight line with that interior angle.
$x = 65^{\circ}$, treating the interior $\angle PQR$ as if it were already the exterior angle.
Extending $PQ$ to $S$ is what creates $\angle P = 55^{\circ}$.
$x = 115^{\circ}$ by naming the triangle vertices alone, with no straight-angle step.

teacher.key_rationale: Exterior ∠RQS and interior ∠PQR form a straight line, so x=180°−65°=115°. Taking 65° as the exterior omits the straight-angle step. Saying the extension creates ∠P reverses cause. Naming vertices alone conflates a different task.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote right-triangle source as △PQR with PQ extended to S and exterior angle x at Q.
